title: OS 9 × Swiss Editorial

references.role: actual user UI kit style reference

prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: final high-fidelity CivicSignal MAIN RESEARCH SCREEN concept: "OS 9 × Swiss Editorial".
Primary request: The user has examined their own Mac OS 9 Platinum UI kit and explicitly asks "Modernize it slightly, like OS 9 meets Swiss Editorial". Create one polished desktop application mockup that combines those two references thoughtfully.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET, the existing Swiss Editorial research workspace. Preserve its main functional composition, content, navigation, source types and source inspector. It is the foundation for the editorial grid, numerical section labels and red accents.
Input image 2: STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, a screenshot of the user's actual CHS UI Kit with "OS 9" selected. Borrow its platinum grey surfaces, shallow highlight/shadow bevels, 1px outlines, near-square corners, restrained violet/grey-era feel, compact controls and Chicago-flavoured small headings. Do not copy its component catalogue content or side navigation labels.
The hybrid should read as a contemporary, expertly designed daily-use research tool with OS 9 ancestry. Modernize SLIGHTLY: keep the recognizable platinum material and fine bevel language; modern readability and Swiss editorial hierarchy take priority over exaggerated nostalgia.

DESIGN SPECIFICATION:
- Full single flat landscape desktop viewport around 16:10, head-on, all edges visible, no external presentation background, no laptop or desktop wallpaper.
- Light platinum-grey application chrome and toolbar, with white reading surfaces. A deliberate grey navigation/session region, a large white central research canvas and a neatly docked light-grey source inspector.
- Use near-black Swiss grotesk sans-serif for readable body and UI text. The main "Start with the evidence." heading is bold and assertive but not poster-sized. Chicago-like typography is limited to small panel/titlebar labels. Compact monospace section numbers add the editorial index character.
- One confident vermilion-red accent for the active Research item, citations, section numbers or small selection markers and the Send action. Keep the old violet selection out of the final hybrid so the system feels coherent.
- Fine, calm 1px grey/black rules, carefully aligned columns and strong editorial whitespace. Number the main sections discreetly 01 / Question, 02 / Answer, 03 / Evidence, 04 / Follow-up.
- OS 9 influence is concentrated in thin pinstriped titlebar strips on "Research sessions" and "Source inspector", subtle dual-line inset panel edges, shallow bevelled compact grey buttons, small square disclosure controls, a small inset search/composer field and near-square 2px corners.
- Bevels must be understated, precise and thin. No chunky 3D buttons, no glossy Aqua, no glassmorphism, no traffic-light macOS window buttons, no Apple logo or dock, no torn paper textures.
- Top toolbar remains compact and practical, with a modest titlebar strip reading "CivicSignal / Research". Avoid stacked decorative bars wasting vertical space.
- Keep main reading comfortable with clean high-resolution type. This is neither a pixel-art game nor an austere poster; it is a usable civic research interface.

PRESERVE KEY CONTENT ACCURATELY:
Brand "CivicSignal"; navigation "Research", "Briefs", "Connect", "Embed", "Coverage".
Left session region "Research sessions"; "+ New research"; "Housing policy" selected; "Labour standards"; "Privacy and data".
Toolbar "Across Canada"; "Last 7 days"; "Your model · Connected".
User question "Which federal sources should I inspect on housing?"
Main heading "Start with the evidence."
Answer "Review the legislation, then inspect bill status and debate citations. News headlines add context and link to the publisher." Small red inline citation markers [1] [2] [3].
Evidence section title "Evidence ledger"; a compact ruled table with columns "Source type", "Key source", "What to inspect"; four rows:
"Legislation" / "National Housing Act" / "Official source";
"Bills" / "Housing-related bills" / "Status and identifiers";
"Debates" / "House of Commons" / "Citations and short excerpts";
"News" / "Publisher headlines" / "Headlines and links".
Small line "Retrieved from 4 source types". Source names have a small external-link arrow.
Right inspector "Source inspector"; "National Housing Act"; "Justice Laws Website"; fields "Type / Statute", "Jurisdiction / Federal", "Content / Full section text". Button "Open official source ↗" uses a subtle grey OS 9 bevel with black label and a small red arrow, rather than a huge solid red slab. Note "Unofficial version. Check the official source." Put this in a quiet inset notice.
Coverage rows "Federal records — Available" and "Municipal records — Not covered", with small restrained status dots.
Follow-up field "Ask a follow-up about these sources…" with compact red send button; small command controls "/coverage", "/in-force", "/changes".
Small footer label "OS 9 × SWISS EDITORIAL" and "Design concept · Sample data".
Constraints: no invented legal passages, no extra charts or metrics, no article body text, no fake public officials. Preserve the substance and broad layout of image 1 while reinterpreting its chrome with image 2. Deliver one professional full-screen UI mockup with excellent typography and a clearly visible OS 9/Swiss hybrid identity.
